newsitem.title: USA: U.S. NAPM's Kauffman says industry growing slowly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. NAPM's Kauffman says industry growing slowly.

text.p: Ralph Kauffman, Chairman of the Business Survey Committee of the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM), said the U.S. manufacturing sector is growing, albeit at a slow pace.

"We're still growing slowly," Kauffman told reporters on a teleconference following the release of the NAPM's October report on U.S. manufacturing. "Although, with the Purchasing Managers' Index at 50.2, the manufacturing sector is just barely growing."
Looking ahead, Kauffman said the October NAPM data suggest manufacturing's fourth quarter won't be "tremendously strong."

So far in 1996, Kauffman said demand for manufactured goods has been reasonably strong, but he has observed some slackening off of late. "Overall, there was certainly an upsurge, and now there seems to be some tapering off. That tapering off is showing itself now," he added.
Kauffman said very few, if any, manufacturers believe the economy is going to "go down the drain." In fact, most see continued growth in the industrial sector but at a slower rate, he said.

Turning to the recent rise in the dollar and its potential effect on manufacturing exporters, Kauffman said, "The strengthening we have seen in the dollar apparently has not hurt manufacturers overall to a very great extent."
